options.option_text: School (school = place; physician:patient is professional:recipient of service)
Student (correct: physician treats a patient; teacher teaches a student — professional and the person they serve ✓)
Book (book = tool; not the person a teacher serves)
Classroom (place, not a person)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: professional → person they serve. Physician serves (treats) a Patient. Teacher serves (educates) a Student. The analogy is about professional role and their primary recipient.

options.option_text: Bones (wrong: bones = orthopaedics)
Heart (correct: oculist treats eyes; cardiologist treats the heart ✓)
Skin (wrong: skin = dermatology)
Lungs (wrong: lungs = pulmonology)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: specialist → organ/system they treat. Oculist = eye specialist; Cardiologist = heart specialist. Medical specialties: oculist/ophthalmologist (eyes), cardiologist (heart), dermatologist (skin), pulmonologist (lungs), orthopaedist (bones).

options.option_text: Dark (wrong: dark is related to light, not transparency)
Transparent (correct: dense:sparse = antonyms; opaque = not transparent; its opposite = transparent ✓)
Thick (wrong: thick is related to density, not opacity)
Heavy (wrong: not the antonym of opaque)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: word : its antonym. Dense : Sparse (thick/crowded : thin/scattered). Opaque : Transparent (blocking light : allowing light through). Antonym pairs in analogies are very common.

options.option_text: Hospital (hospital = place, not a person)
Surgeon (correct: hammer is the carpenter's primary tool; scalpel is the surgeon's primary tool ✓)
Medicine (medicine = what a doctor prescribes, not a scalpel's user)
Patient (patient = who is operated on, not who uses the scalpel)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: tool → professional who uses it. Hammer → Carpenter. Scalpel → Surgeon. Tools and their users: hammer (carpenter), scalpel (surgeon), stethoscope (physician), chisel (sculptor/woodworker), baton (conductor/police officer).

options.option_text: Library (library = place; not the whole of which chapter is a part)
Book (correct: petal is a part of flower; chapter is a part of book ✓)
Page (page is a part of chapter/book, not the whole)
Author (author writes a book; not a part-whole relationship)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: part → whole (synecdoche). Petal is a part of Flower. Chapter is a part of Book. Part-to-whole analogies: petal:flower, chapter:book, cell:organism, room:house, page:book (but chapter is larger than page).

options.option_text: Philosophy (philatelist is not a philosopher — different root)
Stamps (correct: penologist studies prisons; philatelist collects/studies postage stamps ✓)
Coins (coins = numismatics, not philately)
Languages (wrong: linguistics or polyglot, not philatelist)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: expert/collector → their area. Penologist studies prisons/punishment. Philatelist collects/studies postage stamps. Other specialists: numismatist (coins), lepidopterist (butterflies), ornithologist (birds), entomologist (insects).

options.option_text: Social (synonym of gregarious — not an antonym)
Misanthropic (correct: sanguine:pessimistic = optimistic:opposite; gregarious = sociable; its opposite = unsociable/misanthropic or introverted ✓)
Generous (not the antonym of gregarious)
Loquacious (wrong: loquacious = talkative; not the antonym of gregarious)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: word : its antonym. Sanguine (optimistic) : Pessimistic (opposite). Gregarious (sociable, loves company) : Misanthropic (hating/avoiding people). MISANTHROPIC = showing a dislike of other people and human society.

options.option_text: Chaos (synonym of turbulence — not an antonym)
Tranquility (correct: ignominy:honour = shame:dignity = antonyms; turbulence:tranquility = disturbance:calm = antonyms ✓)
Storm (synonym-related, not antonym)
Flight (turbulence occurs during flight — causal, not antonymous)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: word : antonym. Ignominy (public shame/disgrace) : Honour (respect/dignity) — antonyms. Turbulence (violent disturbance) : Tranquility (calm, peace) — antonyms.

options.option_text: Fish (wrong: tadpoles become frogs, not fish)
Frog (correct: caterpillar metamorphoses into butterfly; tadpole metamorphoses into frog ✓)
Toad (wrong: tadpoles become frogs; toads develop from toad eggs with a slightly different tadpole form)
Dragonfly (wrong: dragonfly comes from a nymph/larva, not a tadpole)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: larval/immature form → adult form (metamorphosis). Caterpillar → Butterfly. Tadpole → Frog. Other metamorphosis pairs: larva → beetle/fly; nymph → dragonfly; kitten (growing, not metamorphosis); egg → chick.

options.option_text: Miserliness (synonym of parsimony — not the antonym)
Generosity (correct: mendacity:truthfulness = lying:honesty = antonyms; parsimony:generosity = stinginess:openhandedness = antonyms ✓)
Frugality (synonym of parsimony — not an antonym)
Thriftiness (synonym of parsimony — same meaning)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: antonym pairs. Mendacity (habitual dishonesty/lying) : Truthfulness (honesty). Parsimony (extreme unwillingness to spend money) : Generosity (willingness to give freely). Both pairs are antonyms: lies↔truth; stinginess↔generosity.
